title: Introduce delta-assertor and release-signature-compiler for intake pipelines
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds a deterministic change classifier (delta-assertor) to reduce noisy churn in model metadata and a release-signature-compiler that compiles signed deltas into concise changelog snippets and confidence scores. Backwards compatible; exposes opt-in CLI flag for early adopters. Includes unit + integration tests and a release-note generation job for the intake pipeline.
description:
Context & motivation:
Onboard metadata churn has been a recurring source of noisy release notes and spurious changelog entries in the model registry. Small edits in ancillary fields (uploader notes, transient tags) caused the current changelog synthesizer to emit high-volume, low-signal entries and made reviewers ignore release briefs. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) delta-assertor, a deterministic change classifier that normalizes and scores diffs between model profile versions; (2) release-signature-compiler, a post-assertor job that composes changelog snippets from signed deltas and attaches a confidence and why-summary for reviewers and the auto-release flow.

What this PR delivers:
- delta-assertor: a lightweight library + CLI that consumes two profile JSONs and emits a signed delta artifact containing: semantic change category (schema, weights, perf, docs), normalized field-level diffs, a delta fingerprint, and a compact human-readable rationale. Determinism ensured via canonical JSON canonicalization and stable hashing.
- release-signature-compiler: a pipeline step that consumes signed deltas and renders one-line and paragraph release blurb candidates with confidence scores and optional automated release-note drafts. Integrates with the existing release-drafter flow and can be toggled per-collection.
- Opt-in onboarding flag: `onboard --assert-delta` to produce signed delta artifacts during intake so that downstream reviewers and CI can gate on meaningful deltas.
- Tests: unit tests for diff heuristics, integration tests in the fixture registry, and an end-to-end smoke test that simulates a model metadata bump and ensures only meaningful deltas trigger release blurb generation.
- Docs: docs/registry/delta-assertor.md with developer notes and operational guidance, and a short playbook for handling low-confidence deltas.

Checklist:
- [x] delta classification algorithm and canonicalization implemented
- [x] signing scheme and validation hooks added (KMS-backed signing emulation in dev)
- [x] release-compiler templates and confidence heuristics implemented
- [x] unit + integration tests added and passing
- [x] docs and quickstart updated
- [x] migration guide for QA and platform teams

High-level commits (summary):
- commit 1: introduce delta-assertor library, classifiers, and canonicalizer (python)
- commit 2: add onboarding CLI flag and plumbing to intake service to emit delta artifacts
- commit 3: implement release-signature-compiler and templates (go service)
- commit 4: add KMS-signing compatibility layer and test harness
- commit 5: add unit and integration tests + e2e smoke test
- commit 6: docs and examples + changelog generator CI job
- commit 7: minor fixes from review (stability/timeout tuning)

Files/areas changed (high level):
- services/intake/src/delta_assertor.py (new)
- services/intake/cli.py (opt-in flag wiring)
- services/release-compiler/main.go (new) and templates/release_templates.yaml
- infra/ci/workflows/e2e-delta.yml (new job)
- docs/registry/delta-assertor.md (new)
- tests/fixtures/model_profiles/*.json (new fixtures)
- tests/integration/test_delta_assertor.py (new)

Review conversation (selected):
- Alex Rivers (reviewer): "Why not reuse the existing change-scorer? The heuristics look similar."
  - Author: "We experimented with the change-scorer; delta-assertor uses canonicalization + field whitelisting and a compact rationale structure which avoids several classes of false positives we saw in prod. The code imports the scoring primitives where appropriate and adds a lightweight canonicalizer not present in the scorer."
- Priya Patel: "How do we handle signed deltas for private deployments where KMS is customer-managed?"
  - Author: "Signing is pluggable — default CI uses dev-KMS emulator. The production path supports an external KMS provider; docs include the YAML snippets for binding customer KMS to the signing service. We added validation hooks that will skip signature verification if the tenant opts out (still emits unsigned delta)."
- Jonas Müller: "Can the compiler accidentally create misleading release notes (overstating perf wins)?"
  - Author: "We use conservative thresholds for automatic wording. Any delta with perf changes above 5% is flagged for manual review and the compiler will emit a 'candidate' label; only high-confidence deltas (confidence >= 0.85) are eligible for auto-draft inclusion. The test-suite includes synthetic perf deltas to verify behavior."
- Alex Rivers: "Minor: the canonicalizer needs a stable ordering for map keys; use json-stable-stringify lib or our util."
  - Author: "Addressed in commit 7 — switched to the shared util and added a test asserting stable ordering."

CI summary:
- CI run #7123: lint (pass), unit (pass), integration (fail flaky test test_onboard_timeout) — rerun triggered by author; subsequent run passed. e2e job (e2e-delta) run on feature branch in staging passed. Code coverage for services/intake up ~3%.

Migration and rollout plan:
- Week 1 (canary): enable `--assert-delta` for 10% of onboard traffic (internal only). Collect delta volume reduction, false-positive rate, and reviewer feedback.
- Week 2: enable compiler auto-drafts for high-confidence deltas only and wire the CI job to attach artifact to Linear tasks created by the intake flow.
- Week 3: open rollout to all onboarding flows if metrics show >50% reduction in low-signal changelog entries without missed perf regressions.

Operational notes:
- Signed deltas are stored in `s3://registry-deltas/{collection}/{delta-fingerprint}.json` with 90-day retention by default.
- The delta-assertor has a 150ms median latency in microbenchmarks; release-compiler runs as a separate async job to avoid intake latency coupling.

Backwards compatibility and opt-in nature:
- The new flow is opt-in via CLI flag and collection-level config; default behavior remains unchanged. The release-signature-compiler can be turned on independently and reads existing profile history to synthesize deltas.

Merge outcome:
- Approved by reviewers (Alex Rivers, Priya Patel, Jonas Müller). Merged via squash on 2024-10-15 by release-bot.

Follow-ups (future work):
- Add lightweight UI in Console to inspect signed deltas and rationale.
- Tune perf thresholds and calibration using active traffic in canary.
- Hook compiler output to automated changelog translation/summary for external release notes.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps the default onboarding behavior unchanged and provides strong opt-in controls for early testing. Signed delta artifacts can be used later for audit and rollback triggers.
